title: The coefficient algebra module structure and canonical coefficient map on Tor
statement: Let $R\to A\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, with the composite $R\to B$, let $M$ be an $R$-module, and let $n\geq0$. Use $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)$ of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. The functor in the coefficient module is additive. Regard this existing Tor group as an $A$-module by letting $a\in A$ act by the functorial image of the $R$-linear coefficient endomorphism $b\mapsto ab$ of $B$. This specifies the action, rather than choosing an arbitrary module structure. For another commutative $A$-algebra $C$, with its composite $R$-algebra structure, and an $A$-algebra homomorphism $f:B\to C$, the canonical coefficient map $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)\to\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,C)$ is the functorial map induced by the underlying $R$-linear map of $f$; it is $A$-linear. In particular, $B=A$ defines the coefficient $A$-module $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)$.
